sections.label: Maintenance of Racial Harmony Bill powers
sections.summary: The Bill consolidates existing powers against conduct threatening racial harmony, though it cannot force races to get along or prevent racist slights.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: At present, dealing with the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Bill, there are powers to deal with conduct which threatens racial harmony, but what you see is that they are found in different pieces of legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What this Bill does is to bring those powers together in one place.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Based on the responses we have had from members of the public when we had our consultations and when we put out the Bill, I want to make one point.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This Bill is not a panacea for all racial issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You cannot by law force people of different races to get along with one another, nor can you prevent insensitivity or racist slights from happening in everyday interactions by passing a law.

sections.label: MHA press release on proposals
sections.summary: MHA's press release and Annex 1 state that most substantive proposals in the Bill are not new.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The point that has been made by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) through its press release, which I am sure the Members who are intending to speak on the Bill would have looked at, and which I would emphasise again and you will see it from Annex 1 is that most of the proposals in this Bill – certainly the substantive proposals – are not new.

sections.label: Tensions lasting 17 days
sections.summary: The tensions lasted 17 days before stabilising, with 23 people dead and more than 400 injured.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That was the state of the tensions at that point.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It lasted 17 days before the situation stabilised; 23 people died, more than 400 were injured.

sections.label: Second time calm in 12 days
sections.summary: The second time, calm was established after 12 days, with 13 dead and more than a hundred injured.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The second time round, it took 12 days before calm was established; 13 people died and more than a hundred were injured.

sections.label: Presidential Council for Minority Rights veto
sections.summary: The Presidential Council for Minority Rights can veto any legislation Parliament passes that it feels affects minorities' rights and privileges.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Presidential Council for Minority Rights can veto any legislation that Parliament passes that it feels affects the rights and privileges of minorities in Singapore.

sections.label: Surveys on Singapore racial harmony
sections.summary: Surveys found 92% said Singapore was a good place for racial minorities and most respondents rated race relations good or very good.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Over the years, our insistence on maintaining racial and religious harmony, and our zero tolerance for bigotry and hatred has made Singapore a very different place compared with others.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If you look at a 2023 Gallup World Poll, 92% of respondents in Singapore said that Singapore was a good place to live in for racial minorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Another global survey by the Pew Research Center in 2021 found that 92% of respondents in Singapore think that having people of different backgrounds, including racial backgrounds, makes Singapore a better place to live in.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Most recently, in August of last year, my Ministry and the Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) polled more than 1,000 Singapore residents on their sentiments towards racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Members will see that the majority of the respondents felt that the current state of race relations in Singapore was good or very good.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: About half agreed that Singapore's laws were adequate to protect racial harmony, 6% disagreed and the rest were somewhere in-between.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Most agreed that it was both the Government's and the community's responsibility to strengthen race relations.

sections.label: France black racial discrimination report
sections.summary: A 2023 report found 91% of black people in France had been victims of racial discrimination often or from time to time.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You get the sense that racial issues continue to be flashpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And if you turn to France, a report that was published in 2023 found that 91%, more than nine in 10 of black people had been victims of racial discrimination either "often" or "from time to time".

sections.label: US segregated neighbourhoods study
sections.summary: A 2021 University of California study found racially segregated US residential neighbourhoods remain the lynchpin sustaining systemic racial inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The University of California did a study in 2021 and found that racially segregated residential neighbourhoods in the US remain the "lynchpin" that sustains systemic racial inequality.

sections.label: French banlieues population share
sections.summary: About five million people, roughly 8% of the French population, live in areas classified as banlieues.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Around five million people, or about 8% of the French population, live in areas classified as banlieues.

sections.label: IPS housing estate racial mix survey
sections.summary: A 2024 IPS survey found 93% of respondents agreed it was important to have a mix of races in each housing estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) conducted a survey in 2024 and 93% of the respondents agreed that it was important to have a mix of people from different races in each housing estate.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Bill race discrimination
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness Bill prohibits workplace discrimination based on some characteristics, including race.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Most recently, the Workplace Fairness Bill prohibits workplace discrimination based on some characteristics, including race.

sections.label: Singapore race relations harmony surveys
sections.summary: MHA and MDDI polling found over 85% felt race relations better or same, while an IPS and OnePeople.sg study found 65.4% rated harmony high.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The poll that MHA and MDDI conducted last year, it found that over 85% of respondents felt that race relations are better or the same compared to 10 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: IPS and OnePeople.sg, also conducted a study based on a survey last year involving 4,000 Singaporean residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This study found that nearly two-thirds, 65.4%, of respondents rated Singapore's racial and religious harmony as high or very high.

sections.label: Race offences and Community Remedial Initiative
sections.summary: It brings over existing race-related Penal Code offences and introduces the Community Remedial Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: First, it brings over existing race-related offences in the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, it introduces the Community Remedial Initiative (CRI).

sections.label: Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony
sections.summary: It establishes the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony to advise on matters referred by the Minister for Home Affairs or Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Fourth, it establishes the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony to advise on matters relating to racial and religious harmony that are referred to it by the Minister for Home Affairs or by Parliament.

sections.label: Community Remedial programmes as prosecution alternative
sections.summary: Criminal prosecution may be necessary but cannot mend community ties, so an offender might be offered Community Remedial programmes as an alternative to prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And criminal prosecution may be necessary, but it cannot, by itself, mend the community ties.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Thus, if you have an offender, he might be offered an opportunity to participate in Community Remedial programmes as an alternative to prosecution.

sections.label: Minister appoints community partners for programmes
sections.summary: Clause 41(2) provides for the Minister to appoint community partners to deliver programmes, and MHA intends to work with OnePeople.sg and MCCY to design them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Clause 41(2) of the Bill provides for the Minister to appoint community partners to deliver the programmes and MHA intends to work with OnePeople.sg and the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) to design suitable programmes based on the context of the different types of offensive conduct.

sections.label: Guided reflection sessions and prosecutorial discretion
sections.summary: It encourages amity through guided reflection sessions, completion is not compulsory, failure can be considered by the Public Prosecutor, and egregious cases will not be offered CRI.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Third, by encouraging amity by arranging guided reflection sessions with the alleged offender and aggrieved individual or community.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But as clause 41(4) provides, it is not compulsory for an alleged offender to complete the programmes, but failure to complete can be taken into account by the Public Prosecutor in exercising prosecutorial discretion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Egregious cases will not be offered the opportunity of CRI so that a clear and strong signal is sent that such conduct will be treated severely.

sections.label: Three remaining proposals in speech
sections.summary: The speech will detail three remaining proposals: a Restraining Order regime, the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony, and safeguards against malicious foreign influence for race-based entities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In my speech, I will provide details on the remaining three proposals: first, establishing a Restraining Order regime to enable the Government to act quickly and pre-emptively against content that threatens racial harmony; second, establishing the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony to advise on matters relating to the maintenance of racial and religious harmony in Singapore; and third, introducing safeguards against malicious foreign influence for race-based entities.

sections.label: Racial content Restraining Orders
sections.summary: Clause 8 lets the Minister for Home Affairs make Restraining Orders against those communicating, producing or distributing content prejudicing racial harmony, with five possible prohibitions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: A 2024 poll conducted by MDDI, involving more than 1,000 Singapore residents, provided three insights: first, one in two respondents have encountered content in the online space that might be considered racist or racially insensitive; second, two in three agreed that allowing racially offensive content to spread could threaten racial harmony; and third, seven in 10 agreed with the need for racially offensive content to be removed as quickly as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Government shares the view that there should be levers to quickly remove content that could undermine our racial harmony and prevent such content from being further disseminated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Therefore, clause 8 of the Bill will enable the Minister for Home Affairs to make Restraining Orders against persons involved in the communication, production or distribution of content that prejudices the maintenance of racial harmony in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Specifically, a racial content Restraining Order under the Bill may do one or more of the following: (a) prohibit a person from communicating or distributing specified information or material; (b) prohibit a person from addressing a specified audience on a specified subject; (c) require a person to take all reasonably practicable steps to ensure that any specified information or materials are no longer available to the general public in Singapore; (d) prohibit a person from printing, editing, assisting, or contributing to, any publication or a specified publication; and (e) prohibit a person from holding office in an editorial board or committee of any publication.

sections.label: Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony
sections.summary: Clause 3 establishes the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony, replacing the existing Presidential Council for Religious Harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Moving to the next proposal, clause 3 in this Bill will establish the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony, which will replace the existing Presidential Council for Religious Harmony.

sections.label: President's discretionary powers
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Constitution to let the President act in his discretion on Council appointments advice and on confirming, cancelling or varying Restraining Orders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Bill comprises amendments to the Constitution to enable the President to act in his discretion: (a) in deciding whether to act on the Presidential Council for Minority Rights’ advice on Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony appointments; and (b) in confirming, cancelling or varying a Restraining Order in cases where the Cabinet’s advice is different from the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony’s recommendation.

sections.label: Designating race-based associations
sections.summary: Clan associations and business associations linked to the Chinese, Malay and Indian races will be designated first.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In the first instance, we will designate clan associations and business associations linked to the Chinese, Malay and Indian races.

sections.label: Foreign influence donation disclosure
sections.summary: Clauses 18, 19, 20, 23 and 24 introduce baseline measures requiring designated race-based entities to disclose donations from foreign or anonymous sources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Clauses 18, 19, 20, 23 and 24 of the Bill will introduce baseline measures against malicious foreign influence that designated race-based entities will have to comply with.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: First, designated entities will need to disclose donations accepted from foreign or anonymous sources.

sections.label: Leadership citizenship requirements
sections.summary: Designated entities' responsible officers must be Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Fourth, designated entities will need to comply with the following leadership requirements: one, their responsible officers must be Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents (PRs).

sections.label: Minister's foreign influence Restraining Orders
sections.summary: Clause 27 empowers the Minister to issue foreign influence Restraining Orders imposing stepped-up measures on a specific race-based entity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Clause 27 empowers the Minister to issue foreign influence Restraining Orders to impose stepped-up measures on a specific race-based entity.

sections.label: Bill's five key proposals
sections.summary: The Bill aligns race and religion provisions and has five key proposals, including porting Penal Code offences and establishing the CRI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This Bill aligns what we have for both race and religion, since the objectives of the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act also apply in the context of racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This Bill has five key proposals: (a) port over existing race-related offences in the Penal Code; (b) introduce the CRI; (c) establish the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony; (d) establish the Restraining Order regime; and (e) introduce safeguards against foreign influence for race-based entities.

sections.label: Pre-emptive Restraining Order regime
sections.summary: The Restraining Order regime allows pre-emptive action against conduct that could inflame racial tensions before it goes viral.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Restraining Order regime allows us to take action pre-emptively against conduct that has the potential to inflame tensions between racial groups before it goes viral and causes irreparable damage to our social cohesion.

sections.label: Designating clan and business associations
sections.summary: In the first instance, clan associations and business associations linked to the Chinese, Malay and Indian races will be designated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In the first instance, we will designate clan associations and business associations linked to the Chinese, Malay and Indian races.

sections.label: Over 300 entities designated
sections.summary: The designations are estimated to cover more than 300 race-based entities in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Our estimate is that the designations will cover more than 300 race-based entities in the first instance.

sections.label: 14 days for representations
sections.summary: All entities will be informed of MHA's intention to designate them and given 14 days to make representations or seek clarifications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: All entities will be informed of MHA's intention to designate them and will be given 14 days to make representations or seek clarifications before the designation takes place.

sections.label: Burden of proof on accused
sections.summary: The Bill's recurring phrase requires the accused to prove on the balance of probabilities that all reasonable steps were taken, imposing a significant burden on individuals including volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A recurring phrase in the Bill states that "it is for the accused to prove, on the balance of probabilities, that the accused took all reasonable steps to comply." This wording imposes a significant burden of proof on individuals, particularly volunteers who already juggle public service responsibilities.

sections.label: Interaction with FICA
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on how the Bill will interact with the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act passed in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Additionally, I seek clarification on how this Bill will interact with the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act (or FICA) passed in 2021.

sections.label: Encouraged by CRI clause 41
sections.summary: The speaker is particularly encouraged by the CRI in clause 41.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, I am particularly encouraged by the CRI in clause 41.

sections.label: Lessons of racial unrest
sections.summary: The racial unrest and Maria Hertogh riots of the 1950s and 1960s are stark reminders of how fragile harmony can be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The painful lessons of the 1950s and 1960s – the racial unrest, the scars of the Maria Hertogh riots – serve as stark reminders of how fragile harmony can be.

sections.label: Poll findings on racism
sections.summary: The 2023 Gallup World Poll ranked Singapore first among 135 countries for racial minorities, while a 2024 MDDI poll found many still see racism as a problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The 2023 Gallup World Poll ranked us first among 135 countries as a great place for racial minorities to live – 92% of those polled said they felt welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The 2024 MDDI poll also reminds us that nearly half of our fellow Singaporeans still see racism as a problem and more than half have experienced racial insensitivity online.

sections.label: Questions raised in speech
sections.summary: The speaker raised questions on protecting harmony without harming dialogue and freedom of expression, and safeguarding openness without foreign influence undermining unity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Today, I have raised in my speech questions that we must answer together: first, how do we ensure that our efforts to protect harmony does not come at the expense of meaningful, honest dialogue and freedom of expression?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, how do we safeguard our openness to the world without allowing foreign influence to undermine our unity?

sections.label: Empowering guardians of racial harmony
sections.summary: It calls for empowering every Singaporean as an active guardian of harmony and introduces measures on racial discourse, foreign interference and community cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us empower every Singaporean to not just be a passive observer, but an active guardian of the harmony we hold so dear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It introduces measures to regulate racial discourse, counter foreign interference and strengthen community cohesion.

sections.label: Clarifying scope of racial speech law
sections.summary: It asks the Minister to clarify with examples what speech falls within the legislation and whether public racial discussions face legal restriction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since the legislative intent as expressed during this debate may be referenced by the Courts, could the Minister clarify, with specific examples, the types of speech, including the ones I raised, that will or will not fall within the scope of this legislation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm then that members of the public can engage in public discussions on racial issues without an outright legal restriction?

sections.label: Community Remedial programme details
sections.summary: It asks the Minister to share more details on the structure and content of the Community Remedial programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share more details on the structure and content of the Community Remedial programme?

sections.label: Combined versus distinct racial councils
sections.summary: It asks whether a distinct council for racial matters was considered and the rationale for a combined racial and religious council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share if the Ministry considered setting a distinct council for racial matters?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share the rationale for having a combined council for racial and religious matters and how this is preferable to having distinct councils?

sections.label: Presidential powers over Restraining Orders
sections.summary: It states the President's powers when a Restraining Order is first imposed and when it is extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When a Restraining Order is first imposed, the President may cancel, confirm or vary the Restraining Order if the advice of the Cabinet is contrary to the recommendation of the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, when it comes to the extension of a Restraining Order, the President can only cancel a direction or confirm the direction without variation.

sections.label: Rehabilitation for serious race offenders
sections.summary: It asks what programmes are available for rehabilitating serious race offenders who are not eligible for CRI-Race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what programmes are available for the rehabilitation of serious race offenders who are not eligible for CRI-Race?

sections.label: Clarity on prohibited behaviour
sections.summary: The passage seeks greater clarity from the Government on what behaviour or expressions the Bill will prohibit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As such, we seek greater clarity from the Government on the type of behaviour or expressions that will be prohibited under the Bill.

sections.label: POFMA comment and Restraining Order
sections.summary: It asks whether a comment that received a POFMA Correction Direction would attract a Restraining Order under this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While he received a Correction Direction under the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA) for this comment, would that attract a Restraining Order under this Bill?

sections.label: Phrases and Restraining Orders
sections.summary: It asks whether individuals using certain phrases online or offline would face a Restraining Order or prosecution under clause 40.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would individuals who use phrases, such as "from the river to sea, Palestinians will be free", online or offline, now be subject to a Restraining Order under this Bill or prosecuted under clause 40 of the Bill?

sections.label: Restricting racially sensitive discussions
sections.summary: It asks whether the Bill will restrict discussions of racially sensitive topics such as EIP, Malay national servicemen, death row inmates and CMIO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: More critically, will the Bill be used to restrict discussions of racially sensitive topics, such as EIP, the deployment of Malay national servicemen, the racial breakdown of death row inmates or the "Chinese, Malay, Indian and Others" (CMIO) model?

sections.label: Extended Restraining Orders and journalists
sections.summary: It states that because a Restraining Order can be extended for up to two years each time, an editor or journalist could be kept out of work indefinitely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Considering that the Restraining Order can be extended "one or more times" for up to two years each, this means that an editor or journalist could potentially be kept out of his work indefinitely.

sections.label: Existing laws and further curtailment
sections.summary: It says existing laws already limit free expression and asks the Government to explain when Restriction Orders will be issued and what they target.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's existing laws already limited citizens' ability to express themselves freely in many ways and we do not wish to see this Bill to further curtail speeches.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We hope the Government can clearly explain under what circumstances it will issue Restriction Orders and what behaviours or expressions it will target.

sections.label: Existing laws against false speech
sections.summary: The Government already has powers under laws including the Internal Security Act, POFMA and FICA to act against false speech, national security threats and foreign interference.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government already has many powers under laws, such as the Internal Security Act, POFMA and FICA to act against false speech, acts that threaten national security and foreign interference in our politics.

sections.label: PSP support for Bill
sections.summary: PSP will support the Bill despite its reservations, recognising the importance of maintaining racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Recognising the importance of maintaining racial harmony, PSP will support this Bill despite our reservations.

sections.label: Study on racism views
sections.summary: A study found 56% of respondents view racism as an important problem in Singapore, up from 46% in 2016, and about 70% see legislative tools as useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A recent study revealed that 56% of respondents are of the view that racism is an important problem in Singapore, up from 46% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fortunately, a significant majority, about 70%, acknowledges that legislative tools are still useful in safeguarding racial and religious harmony in our society.

sections.label: Calls to revisit race-based policies
sections.summary: Some have called for revisiting race-based or integration policies like CMIO classification, HDB's EIP and Self-Help Groups amid more mixed-race marriages and naturalised and younger Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With more mixed-race marriages, naturalised Singaporeans and younger Singaporeans identifying with a shared identity rather than along ethnic distinctions, some have called for the revisiting of race-based policies or integration policies, like the CMIO classification, the Housing and Development Board's (HDB's) EIP and our Self-Help Groups as well.

sections.label: Clan and business associations inclusion
sections.summary: The Bill automatically includes clan and business associations linked to the Chinese, Malay and Indian races, and MHA stated it is not necessary or desirable for safeguards to apply to all race-based organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, I note the automatic inclusion in this Bill for clan and business associations linked to the Chinese, Malay and Indian races.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourthly, I understand that MHA has stated that at this juncture it is not necessary nor desirable for the safeguards in this Bill to apply to all race-based organisations because they are a much larger and more diverse group.

sections.label: CRI reparative programmes
sections.summary: Clause 41 allows offenders to participate in reparative programmes such as community service or educational workshops as an alternative to custodial sentences or fines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: My next set of clarifications relate to CRI as envisaged under clause 41 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This provision allows offenders to participate in reparative programmes, such as community service or educational workshops, as an alternative to custodial sentences or fines.

sections.label: Tailored CRI programmes
sections.summary: CRI should be tailored to racial sensitivities and could include racial sensitivity workshops, inter-racial community service and dialogue sessions with affected communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope that CRI will be tailored to the specific circumstance depending on the racial sensitivities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It could include structured programmes, such as racial sensitivity workshops, where offenders can engage in facilitated discussions to understand the impact of their actions, the hurt and learn about different cultures; secondly, community service through inter-racial community projects, in order to foster deeper empathy and understanding; and thirdly, dialogue sessions between the offenders and members of the affected community to promote reconciliation.

sections.label: Presidential Council for Racial Harmony
sections.summary: The speaker supports safeguards and the establishment of a special Presidential Council for Racial Harmony to preserve Singapore's multiracial way of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore has long built a harmonious multiracial and multi-religious society and it is our responsibility to work together in preserving our way of life for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I support and agree with the safeguards and the establishment of a special Presidential Council for Racial Harmony.

sections.label: Bill and racial harmony
sections.summary: The Bill shows Singapore's commitment to racial harmony, but its success depends on careful implementation balancing enforcement with education, dialogue and community empowerment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Racial harmony in our nation is integral to our survival and progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill is a testament to Singapore's unwavering commitment to racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, its success will depend on careful implementation, balancing legal enforcement with education, dialogue and community empowerment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We can create a society where racial harmony is not just a policy goal but a lived reality for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: SG60 unity in diversity
sections.summary: The speaker cites 1965 words on multiracial approaches, urges unity in diversity for SG60, declares an honorary adviser role, and notes over 300 entities may be designated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This not only breeds tolerance for different viewpoints but also a readiness to learn and borrow from the accumulated wisdom of other people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We shall, therefore, bring to the world of the UN, the attitude and approaches of a multiracial nation, aware that independence and interdependence of peoples and nations are not incompatible goals to pursue." Those words, Mr Deputy Speaker, echo true since 1965 until today and on the occasion of this year's SG60 of our nation building, let us work together to build a Singapore that is united in its diversity, resilient in its values and steadfast in its pursuit of racial harmony, a shining united light in the sea of global polarising challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I declare that I am an honorary adviser of the Singapore Teochew Poit Ip Huay Kuan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: It was reported that according to MHA's preliminary estimation, this Bill, once passed, will result in the designation of more than 300 such entities in Singapore.

sections.label: Foreign affiliations and donations
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MHA knows the extent of foreign donations to clan and business associations and requests details to understand financial support and risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Clause 19(2)(b) mentions the possibility of "classes of foreign affiliations, if any, that may not be reported".

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask the Minister whether MHA is presently aware of the extent to which our clan and business associations receive donations from foreign counterparts and entities, and if so, to share some details so that we can better understand the extent of such financial support such organisations are currently receiving and have a better appreciation of the likely risks that such organisations may face.

sections.label: Foreign donations not prohibited
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to confirm that foreign-based donations are not prohibited or unwelcome, unlike in FICA, given stiff non-compliance penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This is also bearing in mind the likely penalties which may arise from non-compliance are quite stiff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would further like to ask the Minister to confirm for good order that the presence of foreign-based donations, whether from a foreign counterpart clan or business association or from even a foreign business entity with business interests, is in itself and unlike in FICA not prohibited and not regarded to be unwelcome.

sections.label: Citizens-only rule for designated entities
sections.summary: Speaker asks that responsible offices of designated entities be held only by Singapore Citizens, not PRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In fact, I will go one step further to ask that responsible offices of designated entities must be Singapore Citizens only as opposed to Singapore Citizens and PRs are effectively nationals of another country.

sections.label: Foreign interference aim and reporting burdens
sections.summary: Government aims to reduce foreign political interference in clan and business associations, but speaker worries reporting requirements burden smaller organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Government's aim is to reduce or prevent foreign political interference in local clan associations and business associations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned that the reporting requirements may impose unnecessary administrative burdens on these organisations, especially smaller ones.

sections.label: Clarify foreign donations not prohibited
sections.summary: Speaker asks the Minister to clarify that foreign donations are not unwelcome or universally prohibited, unlike FICA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, I also would like to ask the Minister to clarify that foreign donations themselves are not unwelcome or universally prohibited, because this is not like FICA.

sections.label: Support for Bill despite concerns
sections.summary: Speaker hopes MHA follow-ups on declared foreign entities will not prejudice foreign donations, and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Of course, MHA may follow up on declared foreign entities when deemed necessary, but I hope that this will not lead to unnecessary prejudice against foreign donations themselves. : My Deputy Speaker, notwithstanding my concerns and questions, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Race-based entities and chambers of commerce
sections.summary: Bill allows designation of race-based entities with foreign affiliation restrictions, but it is unclear whether chambers of commerce fall under this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill states that organisations promoting the interests of specific racial groups may be designated as race-based entities, subjecting them to restrictions on foreign affiliations, mandatory disclosures and leadership requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is unclear whether local or foreign chambers of commerce and business trade associations, which primarily focus on trade facilitation, investment promotion and industry collaboration, would fall under this classification.

sections.label: Foreign trade association funding sources
sections.summary: Some foreign trade associations receive funding from overseas business networks, foundations, corporate sponsorships and foreign company membership fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some foreign trade associations receive funding from overseas business networks, foundations, corporate sponsorships and membership fees from foreign companies.

sections.label: Leadership restrictions on governing body members
sections.summary: A clarification concerns leadership restrictions requiring more than 50% of governing body members to be Singapore Citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My third clarification is in relation to leadership restrictions requiring more than 50% of governing body members to be Singapore Citizens.

sections.label: Assurances to trade associations
sections.summary: Singapore is recognised as a trusted hub for trade and investment, and assurances should be given to trade associations and foreign chambers of commerce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, Singapore has been recognised as a trusted hub for trade and investment, with a strong reputation for regulatory clarity and openness to global partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we implement this Bill, let us give assurances to our trade associations and foreign chambers of commerce such that they can continue to play their role in strengthening business ties and facilitating international collaboration.

sections.label: Restraining Orders and foreign influence
sections.summary: The Bill modernises offences, gives the Minister for Home Affairs power to issue Restraining Orders, and curtails foreign influence in race-based organisations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Besides porting over and modernising existing offences, it also gives new powers to the Minister for Home Affairs to issue Restraining Orders to prevent the communication of content considered to be prejudicial to racial harmony in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill further seeks to curtail foreign influence in race-based organisations, such as clans, through requirements such as reporting foreign donations and foreign participation in these organisations.

sections.label: EP discretion over Restraining Orders
sections.summary: If passed, the EP will have discretion to confirm, cancel or vary any Restraining Order made by the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If passed, the EP will have discretion to decide whether to confirm, cancel or vary any Restraining Order made by the Minister.

sections.label: President and racial affairs polarisation
sections.summary: The President taking a position on racial affairs could lead to the presidency being polarised along racial lines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the President to enter the fray and to take a position on racial affairs could quite possibly lead to the presidency being polarised along racial lines.

sections.label: Concerns over presidency and racial issues
sections.summary: The speaker raises concerns about the President's involvement in race-based matters, opposes the EP's discretion provisions, but supports the Bill's wider objectives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, will the presidency then become an arena in which racial issues are fought over?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is mainly due to the potential gridlock it may cause to a newly elected Government if it should require to use past reserves, or when it needs to make key appointments in the public service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the purposes of today's debate, we are further concerned about the implications of bringing the President into decisions involving race-based matters, for the reasons I have given.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On my part, I would emphasise that we are not supportive of the provisions dealing with the EP's discretion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, as stated by my colleagues earlier, we support the wider objectives of managing race relations and will vote in support of the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These are important and crucial updates to our current legislation to uphold racial harmony in an increasingly polarised global environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This will support law enforcement and enhance clarity for the public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, having two separate pieces of legislation for racial and religious harmony may prove to be confusing for the general public as well as for organisations.

sections.label: Board diversity and unity Bills
sections.summary: The 2025 Board Diversity Index reported a fall in boards with at least one-third non-majority culture directors, and the Bills set safety parameters for respectful interactions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The latest 2025 Board Diversity Index reported that the percentage of boards which have at least one-third of directors from a non-majority culture fell.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We need to remain vigilant and be on guard against attempts to weaken or harm our hard-earned unity among different racial groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These Bills are timely and will help to set the safety parameters for respectful interactions and build greater understanding.

sections.label: Arts representation on Presidential Council
sections.summary: The Member asks if the Minister can assure the arts community that the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony will include arts sector representatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, I would like to ask if the Minister can provide some assurance to the arts community that the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony will be composed of some representatives from the literary, visual, performing and musical arts sectors?

sections.label: Council powers and public deliberations
sections.summary: The Member asks for confirmation that specialist opinions will be obtained on artistic work and whether Council deliberations will be made public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clause 33(5)(a) of the Bill alludes to the Council having the power to invite “any person” to attend before it and I believe that it would provide much assurance to the arts community if the Minister can confirm that specialist opinions will be obtained where artistic work and content is concerned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, can the Minister clarify whether there will be opportunities for the deliberations of the Council to be made public and if so, what the frequency of disclosure is expected to be?

sections.label: Examples of harmful content
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Ministry will release examples of harmful content potentially subject to Restraining Orders under clause 8.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My fourth question is on whether the Ministry will be releasing examples of what constitutes harmful content that would potentially be subject to Restraining Orders under clause 8 of the Bill.

sections.label: Definition of information and material
sections.summary: The definition of information and material at clause 8(8) appears wide enough to cover visual, literary, musical and performance art works.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The definition of “information and material” at clause 8(8) appears to be wide enough to cover visual, literary, musical and performance art works.

sections.label: Interpretation of clause 40
sections.summary: The Member's sixth and last question concerns the interpretation of clause 40 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My sixth and last question has to do with the interpretation of clause 40 of the Bill.

sections.label: Arts funding and clause 40(6) defence
sections.summary: The passage states that audience interpretation may make it hard for artists to rely on the clause 40(6) defence, after $100 million was committed to the arts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong committed an additional $100 million of funding to support the arts in recognition of this value that it has in our society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the context of this Bill, however, the element of audience interpretation can make it challenging for an artist to definitively prove that their work is intended as a call for change, rather than being misinterpreted as an endorsement of the very issues that the work seeks to critique.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This ambiguity may then make it difficult for artists to rely on the defence provided at clause 40(6) of the Bill.

sections.label: Australia defence and clause 40(6) guidance
sections.summary: The passage notes Australia's Racial Hatred Act defence, says the Bill does not go as far, and seeks broad interpretation of clause 40(6) phrases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Australia’s Racial Hatred Act introduced in October 1995, for example, provides a defence where a person's conduct was done reasonably and in good faith in the performance, exhibition or distribution of an artistic work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposed Bill today does not go as far as that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, some guidance on the interpretation of clause 40(6) will be helpful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I know it is not possible for the Ministry to provide an exhaustive list of guidelines on this point, but I hope that the Minister can assure us that the terms “good faith” and “bring(ing) about the removal of those matters”, as these phrases are set out in clause 40(6), that these phrases will be broadly interpreted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our artists play a very important role in facilitating this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is essential to strike a balance between preventing harmful content and allowing the arts to thrive as a platform for meaningful discourse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Together with the related Constitution (Amendment) Bill, this legislation strengthens our efforts to uphold racial harmony, ensuring that Singapore remains an inclusive and cohesive society for all.

sections.label: Minister's Restraining Orders power
sections.summary: The passage states that the Bill grants the Minister the power to issue Restraining Orders with immediate effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, the Bill grants the Minister the power to issue Restraining Orders with immediate effect.

sections.label: Remedial CRI race programme alternative
sections.summary: The passage states that participation in the remedial CRI race programme is presented as an alternative to prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Three, participation in the remedial CRI race programme is presented as an alternative to prosecution.

sections.label: Disclosure for race-based entities
sections.summary: The passage states that the Bill mandates disclosure requirements for race-based entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Five, the Bill mandates disclosure requirements for race-based entities.

sections.label: Maintenance of Racial Harmony Bill purpose
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill prevents hostility and hatred between races and makes inciting racial discord an offence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The peace of our nation and society is our responsibility and we must have the will and courage to reach across the divide, get to know each other better and forge a united vision to ensure the peace and progress of our nation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Maintenance of Racial Harmony Bill is important in preventing hostility and hatred from emerging between the different races.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It also makes it an offence to incite and foment discord on the basis of race.

sections.label: Bill prevents foreign influence
sections.summary: The Bill affirms measures to prevent foreign influence and interference in local racial issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The importance of this Bill is also that it affirms measures that will prevent foreign influence and interference in local racial issues.

sections.label: Ethnic self-help groups definition
sections.summary: The question asks whether ethnic-based self-help groups fall within the definition of potential entities under clause 15(A).

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would ethnic-based self-help groups, like the Chinese Development Assistance Council, Yayasan MENDAKI, Singapore Indian Development Association and the Eurasian Association also fall within this definition of such potential entities as per clause 15(A)?

sections.label: Minister establishes CRI
sections.summary: The Bill allows the Minister to establish CRI to address racial incidents and as an alternative to criminal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill also allows the Minister to establish CRI to address racial incidents and as an alternative to criminal proceedings.

sections.label: MHA MDDI racism survey
sections.summary: The study by MHA and MDDI indicates that 43% of surveyed Singaporeans feel racism remains a problem and 35% have had racially insensitive encounters.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As highlighted by the Minister earlier, the study conducted by MHA and MDDI indicates that 43% of surveyed Singaporeans feel that "racism remains a problem in Singapore" and 35% have had "racially insensitive encounters".

sections.label: CRIs and foreign influence order
sections.summary: The MHA press release states CRIs let offenders learn and make amends, completion can affect prosecution, and the Bill allows a foreign influence restraining order.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As noted in the MHA press release dated 7 January 2025, and I quote: "CRIs will provide an alleged offender the opportunity to learn from and make amends for   racist conduct, thereby soothing communal tensions and repairing ties between the communities." And "satisfactory completion of a Community Remedial programme can be taken into account by the Public Prosecutor in deciding whether to prosecute a race-related offence under the Bill." Mr Speaker, I support the establishment of CRIs and would like to know what mechanisms are in place to ensure that the initiatives will be: co-developed with relevant community members and leaders; evidence-based and independently evaluated; and sufficiently funded and staffed by people with the necessary expertise and experience.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill allows the Minister to make a "foreign influence restraining order" if "necessary or expedient to pre-empt, prevent or reduce any foreign influence that may undermine racial harmony in Singapore and present a threat to public peace and public order in Singapore".

sections.label: Online racial material mechanisms
sections.summary: The question asks what mechanisms exist to prevent, monitor or take down online racially problematic material and to support victims.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This material is notoriously difficult to respond to and I would like to know what mechanisms are in place to enable the Ministry, or other agencies, to prevent, monitor or take down racially problematic material that is online, either domestically or internationally, particularly when that material is posted anonymously or under a pseudonym.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to know what mechanisms are in place to enhance domestic cooperation with international agencies, including law enforcement agencies, in responding to online or overseas issues.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The impact of these behaviours can be substantial and it is important that victims are provided with the appropriate level of professional, trauma-informed support and care.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Victims should also be informed of their right to seek legal advice about potential legal action against liable individuals or entities.

sections.label: Forms of racism
sections.summary: Racism exists in several forms and can be covert or overt, conscious or unconscious, deliberate or accidental.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Racism exists in several forms and can be covert or overt, conscious or unconscious, deliberate or accidental.

sections.label: Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act
sections.summary: The Government is introducing the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act as standalone legislation to deal with threats to racial harmony and signal its importance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this regard, I think it is timely that the Government introduces the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act as a standalone piece of legislation to deal with potential threats to racial harmony and to signal the importance of maintaining racial harmony in Singapore.

sections.label: Remedial initiatives and foreign influence
sections.summary: The community must embrace magnanimity and forgive contrite offenders, and the Bill introduces measures against foreign influence covering donations, affiliations and leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While we can mandate that offenders undergo remedial initiatives, the community must also embrace magnanimity and be willing to forgive the offenders if the offenders are contrite and they demonstrate willingness to make amends and rebuild bridges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This Bill also introduces measures against foreign influence by requiring entities, including unincorporated associations, to abide by rules governing donations, affiliations and leadership.

sections.label: Safeguards for designated entities
sections.summary: More than half of designated entities' governing bodies must be Singaporeans, and the responsible officer must be Singaporean or a PR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Under the provision to safeguard designated entities from foreign influence, more than half of their governing bodies must be Singaporeans and the responsible officer for such entities must be either Singaporeans or PRs.

sections.label: Background checks on leaders
sections.summary: For higher-risk or nationally critical designated entities, the Government could legislate more thorough background checks on proposed leaders before appointment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For designated entities that have a lower risk of foreign influence or are regarded as less nationally critical, the nationality-based restrictions on their governing bodies and leaders proposed by this Bill would suffice as safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, for designated entities that have a higher possibility of being influenced by foreign actors or are regarded as nationally critical if compromised – for example, co-operative societies, trade unions, mutual-benefit organisations, platform worker associations and the like – the Government could legislate more thorough background checks on their proposed leaders before these individuals are appointed into their governing bodies or leadership team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that such background checks would help to provide additional guardrails by restricting local born and naturalised Singaporeans with tangible and established foreign affiliations from holding leadership positions in such designated entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A socially harmonious, cohesive and high-trust society will ultimately strengthen the stability of communities and the resilience of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government is sending a strong signal on the importance of racial harmony with this Bill, because, in the words of someone very dear to me, who once lived through the racial riots of the past, we should "never, ever take Singapore's racial harmony for granted".

sections.label: Penal Code section 298 language
sections.summary: Section 298 of the Penal Code's old language on wounding racial harmony has been replaced with language on insulting, vilifying, denigrating, threatening or abusing another on the basis of race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The old language of section 298 of the Penal Code that made it an offence to "wound racial harmony and feelings of any person" has been replaced with language making it an offence to insult, vilify, denigrate, threaten or abuse another on the basis of race.

sections.label: Restraining Order regime introduction
sections.summary: A Restraining Order regime is introduced, allowing MHA to act swiftly against acts that may threaten racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The first is the introduction of a Restraining Order regime, which allows MHA to act swiftly against acts that may threaten racial harmony.

sections.label: CRI reparative measures option
sections.summary: The CRI gives MHA the option to offer reparative measures in lieu of prosecution to offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The second tool is the CRI, which gives MHA the option to offer reparative measures in lieu of prosecution to offenders.

sections.label: Foreign influence race-based entities
sections.summary: Measures on foreign influence require race-based entities to have leadership primarily of Singapore Citizens and to disclose foreign donations and affiliations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The third set of measures to safeguard racial harmony relates to foreign influence and requires race-based entities to have a leadership composed primarily of Singapore Citizens and to disclose foreign donations and affiliations.

sections.label: Scope of unacceptable conduct
sections.summary: Paragraph three's second sentence and paragraph 12 state the scope of unacceptable conduct and offences remains substantively the same as today.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: First of all, paragraph three, the second sentence: "The scope of unacceptable conduct regarding race relations will remain substantively the same as today.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Paragraph 12 says that "the scope of the offences under the Bill is substantially the same as what is covered in the Penal Code.

sections.label: New Presidential Council powers
sections.summary: What is new is the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony, additional power to issue Restraining Orders and CRIs, and additional remedial orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What is new is really the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony, the additional power to issue Restraining Orders and the CRIs, additional remedial orders.

sections.label: Law alone cannot achieve harmony
sections.summary: The speaker says anyone who thinks the law alone can achieve racial harmony needs their head examined.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If anyone thinks that the law alone can achieve racial harmony, I think that person needs to have their head examined.

sections.label: Poll on race relationship responsibility
sections.summary: An MDDI poll found three in five respondents said Government and community hold equal responsibility to strengthen race relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In a poll conducted by MDDI, three in five respondents said that both the Government and the community hold equal responsibility to strengthen race relationships.

sections.label: President's discretion and Restraining Order lapse
sections.summary: If Cabinet disagrees with the Presidential Council, the President has discretion, and an unconfirmed Restraining Order ceases after 30 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But if the Cabinet disagrees with the Presidential Council for Racial and Religious Harmony, then the President has discretion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And if the President does not confirm the Restraining Order within 30 days of receiving the Council's recommendation, the Restraining Order will cease to have effect.

sections.label: Restraining Orders as pre-emptive measures
sections.summary: Restraining Orders are pre-emptive measures issued when a person is likely to commit or is attempting an act, without investigations and prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Restraining Orders are pre-emptive measures and they may be issued if we know that a person is likely to commit or is attempting to commit an act without having to go through a period of investigations and prosecution to establish the criminal conduct.

sections.label: Bill's 44-day period versus MRHA
sections.summary: The Bill uses 44 days from when a person is issued a Restraining Order, unlike the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act's end period for representations.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Bill has used 44 days, counting from the day the person is issued an Restraining Order, in contrast to the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act, which references the end period for making the representations.

sections.label: No orders under Maintenance Religious Harmony Act
sections.summary: Since 1990, when the Bill became an Act, no order has been issued under the Maintenance Religious Harmony Act, let alone extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Since 1990, when the Bill became an Act, the Maintenance Religious Harmony Act, not one order has been issued under the Maintenance Religious Harmony Act, let alone any order being extended.

sections.label: Preacher's disparaging remarks withdrawn
sections.summary: A preacher made disparaging remarks about Buddhism and Taoism on YouTube, then understood, cooperated, withdrew remarks and posted a new video.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A preacher went on YouTube and talked about Buddhism and Taoism, and made some highly disparaging remarks, said that they are superstitious, and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: My Ministry officials had a chat with the preacher and said this is really not on.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He understood, and he was very cooperative and withdrew his remarks, put out a new video.

sections.label: President as check on Minister
sections.summary: The Government views Parliament and the public as essential checks on the Minister's power, with the elected President as an additional check.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Government's view is that Parliament and the public are essential checks on the Minister's power, but that there is also considerable value in having an additional layer of check through the Presidential Council and the President and that it is appropriate for the President, who is directly elected by the people, to act as a check on this power that can be exercised by the Minister.

sections.label: Penal Code section 298A
sections.summary: Section 298A of the Penal Code criminalises acts knowingly promoting or attempting to promote racial disharmony or enmity between racial groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Section 298A of the Penal Code criminalises acts that knowingly promote or attempts to promote on grounds of race, disharmony, or feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different racial groups.

sections.label: Enforcement of section 298A
sections.summary: Section 298A has been enforced for 17 years, and the restriction is being ported over with a slight narrowing.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The point I made earlier in response to Mr Gerald Giam, section 298A has been enforced for the last 17 years and we know that it was, as far as I can tell, most Members of Parliament or all Members did not have any issues with it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, then the second point that Ms Poa made, that Singaporeans are concerned that the Government will use such powers to further restrict what Singaporeans can do or say.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is a restriction there is in the current law and that restriction is being ported over, in fact, with a slight narrowing.

sections.label: Law remains essentially same
sections.summary: Assessments must be made as to whether law is breached, but the law remains essentially the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Assessments have got to be made as to whether law is breached, but the basic point is the law remains essentially the same.

sections.label: Designating Chinese, Malay, Indian associations
sections.summary: The Government intends to designate only clan and business associations linked to the Chinese, Malay and Indian races.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For a start, we only intend to designate clan and business associations that are linked to the Chinese, Malay and Indian races.

sections.label: 14 days for representations
sections.summary: Designated entities will be given 14 days to submit representations to the competent authority after notification of intended designation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Designated entities will be given 14 days to submit representations to the competent authority after they have been notified of their intended designation.

sections.label: Exemptions from leadership requirements
sections.summary: Entities can appeal for exemption from some requirements, including leadership requirements, and the Ministry will consider exemptions case-by-case if sufficient reason is given.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The entities can appeal to be exempted from some of the requirements, including the leadership requirements and my Ministry will look at them and will be prepared to make exemptions on a case-by-case basis, if sufficient reason is given.

sections.label: Maintenance of Racial Harmony Bill safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill's safeguards balance openness with protection from malicious foreign influence, and designation as a race-based entity does not imply wrongdoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, it is really finding the right balance between remaining open and protecting ourselves from malicious foreign influence and that is what the safeguards in the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Bill seek to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And designation under this Bill as a race-based entity does not imply any wrongdoing.

sections.label: Foreign donations and affiliations declared
sections.summary: Clauses 13(5) and 14 define foreign donation and affiliation; no prohibition or approval is required, and entities only have to declare them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Clauses 13(5) and 14 of the Bill define "foreign donation" and "foreign affiliation".

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There will be no prohibition on accepting these foreign donations or having these foreign affiliations in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: No prior or subsequent approval is required from the Ministry to accept these donations or to continue with these affiliations.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The entities would only have to declare them.

sections.label: FICA designations and account restrictions
sections.summary: In 2024, two politically significant persons were designated under FICA and five social media platforms were directed to block 95 accounts linked to a foreign network.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2024, we designated two politically significant persons under FICA and issued account restriction directions to five social media platforms requiring them to block 95 social media accounts linked to a foreign network.

sections.label: CRI scope and prosecutorial discretion
sections.summary: The CRI applies to conduct potentially disclosing offences under the Bill, is not offered for serious actions like incitement of violence, and is not compulsory.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The current intent is for the CRI to apply to conduct that potentially discloses offences under the Bill, but where the actions are serious, like incitement of violence, then it is not the intention to offer CRIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For those cases, the intention is to prosecute them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And the other point, because this relates to race, the CRI will not be compulsory; but failure to complete the CRI can be considered by the Public Prosecutor in exercising prosecutorial discretion whether to charge or not to charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: MHA will work closely with MCCY, OnePeople.SG and community partners on structuring, delivering and monitoring the outcomes of such programmes.

sections.label: Prison programmes for race-related offences
sections.summary: Psychology-based correctional programmes in prison address offending thinking patterns and behaviour, helping offenders stay away from re-offending as part of rehabilitation and reintegration.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Ng asked what programmes are available for individuals in prison for serious race-related offences, given that they may not be eligible for CRI.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have spoken about it in extenso previously, including psychology-based correctional programmes to help address their thinking patterns related to offending, correct their behaviours, help them to stay away from re-offending – and these all part of the Singapore Prison Services efforts to rehabilitate and re-integrate offenders and try and make them contributing members of society.

sections.label: Government accountable through Parliament
sections.summary: The Government is accountable to Singaporeans through Parliament, whereas the Elected President is not.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Actually, the point I was making was that the Government is accountable to Singaporeans through Parliament whereas the Elected President (EP) is not.

sections.label: Elected President disagreeing with Government
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a confrontation with the Government by the Elected President detracts from his role.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: He earlier mentioned that the Government never takes it for granted that the EP will agree with the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, we have to imagine a situation where the EP will disagree because the Presidential Council has disagreed with the Minister and therefore, the EP is entitled to also take the point that he will not follow the Cabinet's decision and could cancel the Restraining Order issued by the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: If that were to happen, does the Minister not agree that such a confrontation with the Government, by the EP, really detracts from his role?

sections.label: Confrontation over race issues
sections.summary: The speaker says confrontation is uncomfortable and now involves the Elected President possibly confronting the Government on race.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: That already involves confrontation and we have always been very uncomfortable with this problem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: But today, we are faced with an additional dimension and that is that you are envisaging that the EP may have to confront the Government on an issue about race, which goes to the fundamentals of every Singaporean's identity and to social cohesion as well.

sections.label: Restraining Orders relating to race
